ajay: Quick follow-up on the SM gating RFC — noticed L4->generic fallback shows +18% p95 on short sequences (seq_len <= 64). Can we tighten gating without losing L4's qkv/fused attention path? Dropping a small repro + logs below.

maria: Can you paste the repro command and which kernel path was selected? Did you run with fused attention enabled? @infra-bot can you attach the probe logs for that runtime build?

ajay: repro command:
```
./run_infer --model redwood-v1-quant --batch 1 --seq 32 --gpu L4 --enable-fused-attn=true --trace-kernel-select
```
log snippet:
```
[2026-11-12T14:03:21Z] runtime: probe sm_capabilities: L4: has_fast_attn=false, has_fp16_math=true
[2026-11-12T14:03:21Z] kernel_select: chosen_kernel=generic_attn, reason=missing_sm_intrinsic
[2026-11-12T14:03:21Z] perf: p95_tokens_ms=24.1 (+18% vs expected)
```

infra-bot: probe uploaded -> s3://redwood-probes/1817301123/kernel_probe_1817301123.log (tags: L4, repro, short-seq)

kev: Looking at that log, L4 reported missing the SM math intrinsic we use for the fused-attn kernel so runtime fell back to the generic attention path. Two potential approaches: 1) relax the gating heuristic to allow L4 fused-attn for short seqs when only FP16 math is present, or 2) add a lightweight runtime probe that enables per-instance optimized kernels after a quick microbenchmark.

liz: Tradeoffs: forcing L4 fused-attn when the intrinsic isn't present can hurt stability for longer sequences (throughput regressions), but the microbenchmark probe adds ~5ms cold-start per GPU context. Suggest a hybrid: transient per-model gating based on a short probe window + an explicit bias param. Example config snippet:
```
gpu.gating = {
  "probe_window": "64",        // tokens to sample
  "probe_bias": "0.6",        // prefer specialized kernel if score >= bias
  "fallback_threshold": "0.02" // abort if error rate > 2%
}
```
Rationale: small probe keeps latency overhead low, bias lets us tune for p95 vs throughput.

ajay: I prototyped bias=0.6 + probe_window=64. p95 improved from +18% to +3% on short seqs, but I saw sporadic correctness spikes on randomized seeds (~0.1% cases). Likely quantization alignment/pack layout differences between L4-optimized kernels and generic path. Need a checksum compare in probe to detect semantic mismatches.

maria: Agree on checksum. Operationally we should make this opt-in per-model for a canary rollout. Proposed model config field: `prefer_low_latency_gpu_paths: "experimental"` and a console metric to watch: `kernel_switch_rate` + `probe_checksum_failures`. Canary flow: enable on <5% of traffic, monitor p95, error spikes, and embedding divergence.

kev: Also add a stable enum for policies so we don't mix strings in configs. Suggest: `KernelPolicy = {"AUTO", "PREFER_L4_LOW_LAT", "PREFER_H100_HIGH_TP", "FORCE_GENERIC"}`. Runtime will evaluate policy -> probe -> final kernel selection. We'll document semantics in the RFC.

ajay: SGTM. I'll open a follow-up RFC with the perf numbers, checksum results, and a canary rollout plan. Action items: ajay -> RFC + perf appendix, infra -> add probe exporter & checksum metric, eng-runtime -> add KernelPolicy enum + probe hook, devex -> console dashboards for `kernel_switch_rate` and `probe_checksum_failures`.

maria: Thanks — please assign owners in the RFC and tag eng-oncall for the canary window. :thumbsup:

kev: One more note: ensure fallback paths log the selected reason (intrinsic missing vs probe failure) so sales/support can triage customer tickets faster. Logging parity across Dedicated/Private is important.

ajay: Added to action items. I'll include a small log schema in the RFC. Closing thread for now, will drop RFC link when ready.
